properties.areaDesc: Mohave, AZ; Clark, NV
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 1:01PM PDT until October 11 at 4:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
FFWVEF

The National Weather Service in Las Vegas has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Mohave County in northwestern Arizona...
Southeastern Clark County in southern Nevada...

* Until 400 PM PDT /400 PM MST/.

* At 101 PM PDT /101 PM MST/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch
of rain has fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Searchlight, Cottonwood Cove Campground, Cottonwood Cove, Hoover
Dam, Cal-Nev-Ari, Temple Bar Campground, Willow Beach and Temple
Bar.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 4:00 PM PDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 4:00 PM PDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Granite Creek basin in...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 400 PM MST.

* At 100 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Granite Creek basin. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of
rain has fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Granite Creek basin.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Granite Creek basin.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Downtown Prescott and Whipple.

This includes State Route 89 between mile markers 308 and 311...and
between mile markers 314 and 315.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
White Spar Campground and AC Williams Granite Creek Park.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Butte Creek, Bannon Creek, Willow Creek, Granite Creek and Miller
Creek.
properties.instruction: Get out of Granite Creek! Flash flooding is imminent or occurring.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 40 to 45 mph.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Arizona and southeast and southern
California.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM MST /5 PM PDT/ this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Difficult driving conditions, especially for larger
vehicles traveling along roads with crosswinds. Light, unsecured
objects may become airborne.
properties.instruction:
A Wind Advisory means that sustained wind speeds of between 30 and 40
mph are expected, or wind gusts of between 40 and 58 mph. Winds this
strong can make driving difficult, especially for high profile
vehicles.

In addition, strong winds over desert areas could result in briefly
lowered visibilities to well under a mile at times in blowing dust or
blowing sand. Use extra caution.

properties.description:
SMWMHX

The National Weather Service in Newport has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
S of Cape Lookout NC to Surf City NC out to 20 NM...

* Until 445 PM EDT.

* At 356 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located near Ar345, or 11 nm southeast of Bogue
Inlet, moving northeast at 25 knots.

higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

Atlantic Beach, The Center Of Bogue Sound, Salter Path, Beaufort
Inlet, The Vicinity Of Pine Knoll Shores, Ar320, Ar345, Ar315, The
Turning Basin, Ar340, Ar330, The Morehead City-Atlantic Beach
Bridge, and The Vicinity Of Atlantic Beach Bridge.

properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Gulf of America including Dry Tortugas and Rebecca Shoal Channel...

At 354 PM EDT, National Weather Service meteorologists detected a a
strong thunderstorm, capable of producing wind gusts near 30 knots.
This thunderstorm was located over Pulaski Shoal Light. The
thunderstorm was nearly stationary.

Locations that will be affected include...
Pulaski Shoal Light, Fort Jefferson, and Dry Tortugas.
properties.instruction:

rough and confused seas, occasional lightning strikes, and
potentially blinding downpours. Get to a safe port as quickly, and as
safely as possible. When downpours reduce visibility, slow down.

Prepare for rainfall rates up to INSERT RAINFALL RATE inches per
hour. Make sure bilge passages and scuppers are clean of any debris
or obstruction.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 1:55PM MDT until October 11 at 3:15PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
At 155 PM MDT, emergency management reported heavy rain over the
Forsyth Burn Scar. Between 1.5 and 2.25 inches of rain have fallen.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Excessive
rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow. The debris
flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing flash
flooding in and around the Forsyth Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Forsyth Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Pine Valley.

This includes Utah Route 18 between mile markers 26 and 27.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Forsyth Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.areaDesc: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 11 at 12:36PM PDT until October 12 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...A moderate risk for sneaker waves is expected. Short
period north-northwest wind waves will interact with a
building west-northwest long period swell.

* WHERE...The beaches of Douglas, Coos, and Curry counties.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Sneaker waves can run up significantly farther on
beaches than normal, including over rocks and jetties. These
waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and sweep
them into the ocean. The waves can also move logs or other
objects which could crush or trap anyone caught underneath.

* View the hazard area in detail at
https://www.wrh.noaa.gov/map/?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Avoid climbing on rocks and jetties. Stay away from the ocean and
remain out of the water to avoid hazardous conditions.

NWSheadline: BEACH HAZARDS STATEMENT REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH MONDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Martin, FL; St. Lucie, FL
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 3:29PM EDT until October 11 at 6:30PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northern Martin County in east central Florida...
Eastern St. Lucie County in east central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 630 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 328 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has
fallen on already saturated ground.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Port Saint Lucie, Walton, Fort Pierce, Stuart, White City, Saint
Lucie Nuclear Power Plant, Fort Pierce Inlet, Jensen Beach,
Indrio, Sewall's Point, Indian River Estates, Port Saint Lucie
River Park, Fort Pierce South, Saint Lucie West, Fort Pierce
North, Nettles Island, Saint Lucie Airport, Saint Lucie Village
and Tradition.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 630 PM EDT THIS EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Moses Lake Area
properties.headline: Blowing Dust Advisory issued October 11 at 12:26PM PDT until October 11 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Patchy to localized areas of blowing dust expected, with
visibility dropping to between one-quarter and one mile at times.
Northeast winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts of 35 mph.  For the Freeze
Watch, sub-freezing temperatures as low as 29F possible.

* WHERE...Quincy, Othello, Moses Lake, and Ephrata.

* WHEN...For the Blowing Dust Advisory, until 5 PM PDT this
afternoon. For the Freeze Watch, from Monday evening through
Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Hazardous driving conditions due to reduced visibility.
Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other sensitive
vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor plumbing.
properties.instruction:
Be ready for a sudden drop in visibility to a mile or less. If you

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 11 at 3:14PM EDT until October 16 at 9:42PM EDT by NWS Columbia SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in South
Carolina...

Congaree River At Carolina Eastman affecting Richland, Calhoun and
Lexington Counties.

Congaree River At Congaree River at Congaree NP Near Gadsden
affecting Richland and Calhoun Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Congaree River at Congaree River at Congaree NP Near
Gadsden.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon to Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Flooding begins in the Congaree National
Park. This will begin to produce flooding of portions of the lower
boardwalk. At 17.0 feet, The access road to the Sandy Run
subdivision becomes flooded. The lower boardwalk in the Congaree
National Park becomes flooded by Cedar Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:00 PM EDT Sunday the stage was 2.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 14.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Tuesday afternoon to a crest of 17.0 feet Wednesday morning. It
will then fall below flood stage late Thursday evening.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Most flooding deaths occur in vehicles. Never drive through a flooded
roadway or around barricades. Turn around, don't drown.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Monday morning at 800 AM EDT.
